text: What makes a great founder?

A great founder has the judgement to make
sound decisions, recognize opportunities,
and mobilise the resources around them.

A great founder programme should help
participants develop these capabilities while
growing with them.

For me, that means creating a journey
that evolves alongside participants,

from their first day to their
next steps after the programme.

Not everyone will immediately
build the next decacorn,

but they should leave better
equipped to take on that challenge.
Each cohort brings different people,

so I'd start by understanding
what participants hope to get.

This would help us identify common
needs and tailor parts of the programme
accordingly.
Beyond personalized approach,

I'd also focus on developing acumen
through practical experience.

Around 50% of unicorn founders had
previously worked at a startup.

We could bring this experience closer by
giving participants opportunities to shadow
founders or work at a startup,

or alternatively inviting those founders
to bring real challenges for participants.

To understand what makes Founder
Sprint valuable, I spoke with alumni.

They highlighted how much they valued the
people they met and the challenges they

faced together, not just
the knowledge they gained.

Having been in both sides
of entrepreneurship program,

I've seen how these kind of meaningful
interactions create lasting valuable
insights.
But they rarely happen by chance;
they need to be intentionally designed.

In response to this, I'd build a
culture of collaborative learning,

with a weekly rhythm where teams present
their progress and get feedback from peers

who take on different roles,
offering fresh perspectives.

These insights could then be documented
into a shared knowledge repository.

I'd also create a living map of
networks shared by participants, alumni,
and the Founder Sprint team.

This would make existing expertise easier
to discover and help participants utilize
the networks around them.

My experience organising entrepreneurship
events at HUBS has taught me how to
facilitate meaningful interactions.

My product design background also taught
me to consider the entire user journey and
how its different elements work together.

I'd bring both perspectives to help grow
Founder Sprint into a program that brings

strong foundation for the next
generation of ambitious founders.
